title: Dedicated Capacity Intake: SLA Triaging Workbook and Prioritization Heuristic
creator: Isha Patel
description:
Purpose:
Create a reusable workbook + decision heuristic used by PMs and Capacity Ops to intake enterprise Dedicated Capacity requests and return a prioritized SLA and GPU recommendation within 2 business days. The workbook should convert customer-provided signals (qps/tps, token distribution, latency SLO, burst profile, regional constraints, isolation needs, regulatory requirements) into: (1) a recommended reserved throughput profile (tokens/s and sustained vs burst buckets), (2) GPU family recommendation (A100/H100 or equivalent quantized variants), (3) suggested scaling policy (min pool, autoscale triggers, pre-warm and burst credits), and (4) residual risk and follow-up questions.

Scope:
- Non-bug product intake for enterprise customers requesting Dedicated capacity.
- Focus on SLA design (p50/p95/p99 latency targets, availability SLO), reserved throughput sizing, GPU class, and scaling guardrails.
- Output is a populated workbook + short justification note for sales/solutions eng and a scorecard for prioritization.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Engineering implementation of autoscaling changes (will be a follow-up ENG ticket).
- Contract/legal negotiation text.

Why this matters:
We currently manually negotiate dedicated sizing with ad-hoc rules that create long cycles and frequent rework post-provisioning. A standard heuristic will reduce cycle time, align buyer expectations on cost vs latency tradeoffs, and provide gated defaults for burst handling and fallbacks (model variants).
acceptance_criteria: A populated workbook template exists (Google Sheet link in links) with input fields, scoring formulas, and an interpretation panel
The heuristic maps common customer profiles to one of three default SLA bands (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with explicit token/s and GPU family recommendations
A short justification note template (<= 300 words) is available for Sales to attach to capacity proposals
Triage runbook with decision tree and follow-up question checklist is documented in Confluence
Hand-off checklist created for ENG to convert recommendations to provisioning signals (min-pool, max-pool, scale-window, burst-credit model)
notes: Design principles: favor predictable cost over small latency gains for baseline bands; use fallback models for graceful degradation; default to regionally-localized pools when customer needs data residency.
We will adopt a 3-component sizing approach: baseline sustained throughput, burst allowance, and cold-start pre-warm budget.

Risk scoring inputs: burstiness (peak/sustained ratio), latency tightness (p95 target relative to median token generation time), regulatory isolation requirement, multi-model mixing (chat + embeddings in same pool).

GPU class rules (initial): H100 for p95 <= 100ms on LLM-2 style models at >500 tokens/s; A100 for balanced cost/latency at <500 tokens/s; consider quantized LLM variants when cost-sensitive and latency targets allow up to 250ms p95.
decisions: Adopt three SLA bands with explicit numeric defaults (Bronze: 250ms p95, Silver: 150ms p95, Gold: 80ms p95). These numbers are starting points to be validated in pilot customers.
Use token/s sustained + burst credit model (burst window defaults: 5 minutes) rather than pure RPS to better reflect LLM workloads.
Require a security_review_required flag for any intake that requests private VPC or on-prem packaging.
Create a warning for multi-region active-active requests: this will require additional networking and monitoring SLAs and be escalated to Solutions Eng.
next_actions: Prototype workbook and circulate to Solutions Eng and Capacity Ops for feedback (owner: Ethan)
Run three historical customer examples through the workbook to sanity-check recommendations and record divergence (owner: Isha)

Create ENG ticket to accept structured provisioning signals from workbook (expected fields: desired_band, sustained_tokens_per_sec, burst_tokens_per_sec, gpu_family, min_pool, max_pool, prewarm_instances).
Schedule a 60-minute review with Sales Enablement and Solutions checkbox next Monday (2026-03-22).
